reference_answer:
Counts for ONE selected plane must be multiplied by the number of planes in the specified generated list. Fix the unsimplified recursive Gray/Givens backend, let S=2^q>=1, N=2^(q+1)=2S, and L=N(N-1)/2. AdjacentGivens.decomposeSO always EMITS L planes, including harmless zero-angle identity rotations. It is a list-length equality, not a theorem that a particular SO matrix optimally needs L nonidentity gates. Each full-control selected plane on the existing q+1 wires has q controls and emits S RY plus2(S-1) CX records, total3S-2. The exact generated counts are RY=L S, CX=L*2(S-1), G=L(3S-2), with zero opaque-oracle calls. These follow from the actual count equalities, not just a cubic upper bound.

Substituting S=N/2 gives G/N=((N-1)/2)*(3N/2-2). Along N=2,4,8,... this ratio is unbounded, so no fixed constant C bounds THIS backend's emitted count by C N for all widths. More quantitatively, for N>=4, L>=N^2/4 and3N/2-2>=N, hence G>=N^3/4; also G<=3N^3/4=6S^3. Thus this generated family has Theta(N^3) records. The lower comparison was derived from the exact equality for this backend; the source upper-bound theorem G<=6S^3 by itself would not prove nonlinearity or any lower bound.

At q=0,N=2,L=1 the counts are one RY and zero CX, G=1. At q=1,N=4,L=6 they are12 RY and12 CX, G=24, while one selected plane costs only four records. This datum refutes treating one-plane cost four as the whole generated list cost, but does NOT refute every asymptotic linear bound:24=6N at this size. Only the growing-width ratio above supplies that family argument.

Nor does any of this prove a lower bound on optimal SO synthesis or preparation of one chosen state/column. The identity matrix, for example, is SO and has an empty exact circuit, although this unsimplified backend still emits its fixed list and identity-angle records. A different optimizer or architecture is not constrained by the backend's count equality. Full-control coverage must actually enumerate all non-target wires, and plane realization/decomposition are extra semantic obligations beyond the per-plane resource line. In this current source those obligations are supplied separately by decomposeSO_action, selectedStep_matrix/Gray transport and compileSO_eval; they are not absent globally and are not proved merely by reading gate counts.

The count concerns the actual finite exact-angle RY/CX list on q+1 wires and no opaque oracle. It is not arithmetic preprocessing time, a finite-bit angle-synthesis/error bound, hardware routing cost, or an optimal gate lower bound. The correct lesson is to aggregate the generated family under its actual model and keep that claim distinct from optimal necessity.
